trial.title: Effect of Meal Timing During Adjuvant Treatment for Cancer

endpoints.measure: Patient-reported treatment-related toxicities: Average weekly scores
endpoints.time_frame: Assessed weekly from start of intervention through end of intervention (up to approximately 6 months)
endpoints.description: Assessed via Patient-Reported Outcomes version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE v5) toxicities, which is administered weekly throughout intervention and therapy; average scores calculated at each time point, timed to oncologic treatment cycles.

endpoints.time_frame: At end of intervention (at approximately 6 months)
endpoints.description: Relative dose intensity (RDI), defined as delivered/planned dose intensity, will be analyzed both as a continuous outcome (% of delivered vs planned) and as a binary outcome (≥85% vs. \< 85%). Regimen-level RDI will be calculated as the average across drugs or based on the dose-limiting agent.

endpoints.measure: Treatment Delivery: Number of patients completing planned adjuvant therapy without unplanned dose reductions or delays

endpoints.measure: Changes in quality of life (QOL): EORTC QLQ-C30
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline (within 28 days prior to initiation of adjuvant therapy), approximately 2-3 months after treatment initiation, end of treatment (within 6 weeks after completion of adjuvant therapy), and follow-up (6-12 months after completion of treatment)
endpoints.description: Change in quality of life assessed using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30), a validated 30-item instrument measuring global health status/quality of life, functional domains (physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning), and symptom domains. Scores are linearly transformed to a 0-100 scale according to standard scoring guidelines. For global health status and functional scales, higher scores indicate better functioning or quality of life; for symptom scales, higher scores indicate greater symptom burden.

outcome.rationale: Small sample (N=50), heterogeneous cancer types, and lack of direct RCT evidence for TRE during adjuvant chemotherapy create substantial uncertainty. Primary endpoints (toxicity, RDI, completion) have mechanistic rationale but unproven efficacy. Trial likely to show feasibility and some secondary biomarker improvements, but primary clinical benefit uncertain.

value.effect_measure: Mean difference in PRO-CTCAE average weekly scores
value.estimand: Difference in mean patient-reported toxicity scores between TRE and control groups at 6 months, ITT
value.uncertainty: Limited direct evidence for TRE during active chemotherapy; based on survivor studies and indirect mechanisms
value.rationale: TRE shows QOL benefits in cancer survivors (Kleckner ES=0.70) and may reduce toxicity via circadian alignment. Small trial (N=50) and mixed cancer types create uncertainty. Predict modest reduction in patient-reported toxicities.

analysis_trace.content: NCT07524218: Effect of Meal Timing During Adjuvant Treatment for Cancer. Phase NA, randomized parallel trial comparing 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE) vs 12+ hour control eating window during adjuvant systemic therapy for solid tumors. N=50, not yet recruiting. Primary completion expected 2029.

Adults ≥18 with solid tumors receiving curative-intent surgery and planned adjuvant systemic therapy (chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiation). BMI ≥18.5. Mixed cancer types. Expected completion rate ~80% based on similar adherence studies.

TRE (8-hour eating/16-hour fasting) aligns feeding with circadian rhythms, potentially reducing chemotherapy toxicity via metabolic switching, autophagy enhancement, and improved insulin sensitivity. Preclinical evidence supports reduced toxicity; human data in active cancer treatment is limited.

Primary endpoints: PRO-CTCAE toxicities (patient-reported), RDI (dose intensity), therapy completion without reductions/delays. Secondary: clinician-reported toxicities, QOL, PROMIS measures, metabolic biomarkers, microbiome, actigraphy, CGM. Mixed endpoints assessing toxicity, treatment delivery, quality of life, and mechanistic biomarkers.

TRE appears safe in cancer populations based on systematic reviews (67-98% adherence). Main safety concern is nutritional adequacy during chemotherapy; monitoring required. No serious safety signals from prior TRE studies in cancer survivors.

1) Low statistical power (N=50) for binary endpoints. 2) Heterogeneous cancer types reduce precision. 3) Adherence challenges during chemotherapy. 4) Lack of blinding may bias patient-reported outcomes. 5) Missing statistical analysis plan details in protocol.

Evidence sources: (1) Stringer 2024 systematic review (PMC12166167) - TRE feasible in cancer, 67-98% adherence, QOL improvements; (2) Kleckner 2024 RCT (PMC11703331) - TRE reduced fatigue in survivors (ES=0.70); (3) Christensen 2022 protocol (PMC10404477) - TRE during chemotherapy rationale; (4) de Groot 2018 JCO exercise/nutrition trial - RDI improvement with intervention. Evidence role: indirect_direction for toxicity reduction; mechanism_background for metabolic effects. No direct RCT evidence for TRE during active adjuvant therapy with these exact endpoints.

No completed RCTs of TRE specifically during adjuvant chemotherapy with RDI or PRO-CTCAE primary endpoints. TIDIER trial (radiation) and IMPACT-Women (breast cancer chemo) ongoing. Evidence base relies on survivor studies and preclinical data.
